newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends sharply lower.

text.p: Philippine shares slid for the second consecutive day, largely due to foreign selling in blue chip issues, traders said on Thursday.
The composite index settled below its 2,600 support, shedding 63.57 points, or 2.42 percent, at 2,572.80 points.

"There is still that instability in the currency market and some people believe the situation is still tenuous since interest rates remain high," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.

The central bank hoped to make further cuts in interest rates if the currency market continued to stabilise. The bank, however, did not slash its overnight borrowing rate since last Friday when it was cut to 25 percent.
"I saw foreigners on the liquidating path. The pressure is still downwards as there is not much support in terms of good news," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
Meralco B and Ayala Land Inc were among the blue chips that encountered foreign selling.
Ayala Land ended at its intra-day low of 21.75 pesos, lower by 1.25 peso the previous day.
Meralco B was the most actively traded issue, losing 13 pesos, or 9.15 percent to close at 129 pesos.
Despite the sharp losses, turnover was light at 1.62 billion pesos.
All indices fell. Losers pounced gainers 119 to 38 in the broad market with 38 issues unchanged.
Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities, said he expected the market to encounter more sell-offs in the coming days and any rally would be technical and short-term.
